title: Finite-Tor domains for ordinary etale chart adjunctions
statement: Fix a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$. All schemes below are separated and finite type over $k$, and all maps are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings killed by powers of $\ell$, and choose $N=\ell^n\geq1$ annihilating both. On small ordinary etale sites use constant-ring module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] and $T_T=(-)_B=-\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Write $D^b_{ctf}$ for bounded constructible complexes of finite Tor amplitude, as in [det-sp-et-proet-adjunction-transfer], and $R_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_T}R_T$ for $R=A,B$ [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line]. Let $h:U\to V$ be separated of finite type, with a compactification whose middle scheme is in the standing setting. Let $F^{et}_{h,R}=Rr_{*,R}j_{!,R}$ for that compactification [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. Then $F^{et}_{h,R}$ preserves $D^b_{ctf}$ for $R=A,B$. For every standing scheme $T$, comparison inverse image $\nu_T^*$ gives an equivalence $D^b_{ctf}(T_{et},R)\simeq D^b_{ctf}(T_{proet},R)$ preserving and reflecting each Tor interval [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian]. Its canonical tensor comparisons intertwine coefficient extension, inverse image, finite Tate tensor powers and shifts on these subcategories. In particular $T_T$ preserves $D^b_{ctf}$, and for any standing map $u:T'\to T$ and $a\geq0$, $b\in\mathbf Z$, the functor $u^*(-)(a)[b]$ preserves $D^b_{ctf}$.

proof.text: Finite type over the field gives locally Noetherian and compact underlying schemes. For each input choose an ordered Tor interval by widening [i,j] to [min(i,j),j]. Apply the finite-value constructible flat-model theorem to obtain its representative. This includes empty intervals and the zero object.

Give the middle scheme of the chosen compactification its induced k-structure using Compactification.overZ and its finite-type/separated instances. Apply lem-sp-etale-compact-support-tor-window to the proper factor and the chosen flat model. If ell^n kills R, ell^(n+1) also kills 1, including n=0. The last two clauses give bounded constructibility and the Tor interval [min(i,j),j+2e] for exactly the given compactification composite.

View the given k-morphism as a morphism of Over(Spec k). Apply lem-sp-etale-pullback-twist-tor-window to the chosen model. Its final model clauses give bounded constructibility and Tor interval [min(i,j)-b,j-b]. The derived Koszul braiding interchanges the pullback complex and the Tate line, matching etaleChartOperation, which tensors the line on the left.

Use the proved native exact-monoidal Tor comparison DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn_mapDerivedCategory_obj_iff, specialized to comparisonUpperStar. This is the ordinary-module comparison underlying lem-exc-comparison-tor-interval, tests every module sheaf, and needs no coefficient-model transport. Bounded-below full faithfulness of the native comparison, as in thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison, gives fullness and faithfulness on our finite-Tor subcategories. An etale-origin witness for a pro-etale object has finite Tor by reflection; hence the restricted comparison is essentially surjective. Transport the etale chart assertion along chartOperationComparison and the etale-origin isomorphism to obtain the pro-etale chart assertion.

Apply lem-sp-etale-scalar-flat-model to each bounded constructible finite-Tor object in its widened ordered interval. Its last clauses give constructible cohomology and the same Tor interval after arbitrary scalar extension. Testing against the unit gives the required bounded cohomology. For a pro-etale input choose its etale-origin witness, reflect its Tor interval as in the previous step, and transport this scalar preservation using the existing canonical B-linear pbcComparisonReduction, which is exactly the comparison used in chartScalarComparison. No flatness of B over A is assumed.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q03-5366a0021 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: This delivery answers the released human re-split note (8472 chars, 10 steps). The live item is split with Lean but its proof is unchanged, so the delivery is not superseded. Statement, stmt_deps, Lean and unit are identical to live. Nothing cites SGA and nothing is in the dropped list. Every old step has a home. Steps 1 and 4 went to lem-sp-etale-scalar-flat-model, with the Noetherian check kept in item Step 1. Steps 2-3 went to lem-sp-etale-compact-support-tor-window, steps 5-6 to lem-sp-etale-pullback-twist-tor-window (N invertibility kept in item Step 3), and steps 8-10 to lem-sp-etale-chart-comparison-isos. Step 7 stays on det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian. The four new nodes are statement-only and of comparable size (about 1.7k, 1.7k, 1.9k and 2.7k chars), none restates the whole item, and the assembly is 1978 chars. I checked each assembly step's hypotheses. Finite type over a field gives Noetherian and qcqs schemes. The compactification's middle scheme is standing and the coefficient rings are ℓ-primary. N=ℓ^n annihilates A and B and is invertible since p≠ℓ. det-pe needs qcqs X and a Noetherian Λ, which hold. I tested each new statement. Scalar node: Stacks 03TT gives the representative on F^a..F^b and 0GKB keeps it constructible. Z/ℓ²→F_ℓ with K=A[0] gives window [0,0], while F_ℓ[0] over A has infinite Tor amplitude and is correctly excluded. Compact-support node: 0E8I flatness of j_!, plus the uniform fibre cd≤2e of lem-sfb-finite-proper-geometric-cd-bound fed into det-ctf-finite-proper-tor with d=2e. A¹⊂P¹ gives RΓ_c=R(-1)[-2], inside [0,2]. Pullback-twist node: the shift window [a-s,b-s] is correct, and c=0, s=0 recover the u^* clause. Comparison node: 0GLZ, the ringed tensor comparison, comparison-pullback and the root comparison σ, with the c=0 unit case. Advisory: the scalar node overlaps lem-sp-finite-coefficient-input-models, an existing node not compared in the report. I did not re-cite it. It is off the unit route, and its closure (via lem-sp-ringed-site-tor-flat-model→def-wf-tensor-product) would add about 44 trace-formula/Poincaré-duality nodes, such as lem-trf-frobenius-open-square, to the item's batch-5 closure. Maintainer: the prover may reuse its Lean. lem-sp-finite-compact-support-domains is an overlap only (it proves finite Tor by a pro-étale route, with no window), and def-sp-p1-comparison-arrows uses a different twist normalization. Batch-5 flag: lem-amb-finite-root-site-comparison was already cited by the base proof (old Step 10). The trace-formula and Poincaré-duality nodes it reaches are generic: stalk tensor and scalar extension, lisse module objects, local constancy, base change, limit descent, localization, and proper finite-fibre. None of them is a step of the trace formula or of Poincaré duality, so I accept it. The declared tool_uses (finite-type-over-Noetherian and det-pe) are the same as in the landed base and are accepted. No changes.

lean.statement: theorem etaleCtfChartDomain (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (k : Type u) [Field k] [Fact (ringChar k).Prime] [Fact (ringChar k ≠ ℓ)] (R : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing R] [Finite R] (n : ℕ) (hR : ((ℓ ^ n : ℕ) : R) = 0) {U V : Scheme.{u}} [U.Over (Spec (.of k))] [V.Over (Spec (.of k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (U ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (U ↘ Spec (.of k))] [IsSeparated (U ↘ Spec (.of k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (V ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (V ↘ Spec (.of k))] [IsSeparated (V ↘ Spec (.of k))] (h : U ⟶ V) [h.IsOver (Spec (.of k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType h] [QuasiCompact h] [IsSeparated h] (c : Compactification h) {T T' : Scheme.{u}} [T.Over (Spec (.of k))] [T'.Over (Spec (.of k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (T ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (T ↘ Spec (.of k))] [IsSeparated (T ↘ Spec (.of k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (T' ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (T' ↘ Spec (.of k))] [IsSeparated (T' ↘ Spec (.of k))] (u : T' ⟶ T) [u.IsOver (Spec (.of k))] : (∀ K, etaleProperty R U K → etaleProperty R V ((Etale.rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactification (ModuleCat.{u + 1} R) c).obj K)) ∧ (∃ hc : ∀ K, etaleProperty R T K → proEtaleProperty R T ((comparisonUpperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} R) T).mapDerivedCategory.obj K), (comparison R T hc).IsEquivalence) ∧ (∀ K, Etale.DerivedCategory.isBoundedConstructible R T K → ∀ a b : ℤ, a ≤ b → (_root_.DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn (Sheaf T.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} R)) a b K ↔ _root_.DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology T) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} R)) a b ((comparisonUpperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} R) T).mapDerivedCategory.obj K))) ∧ (∀ (a : ℕ) (b : ℤ) K, etaleProperty R T K → etaleProperty R T' ((etaleChartOperation R (ℓ ^ n) hR u a b).obj K)) ∧ (∀ (a : ℕ) (b : ℤ) K, proEtaleProperty R T K → proEtaleProperty R T' ((proEtaleChartOperation R (ℓ ^ n) hR u a b).obj K))
lean.note: The single-coefficient theorem is specialized separately to R=A and R=B with the common annihilating N=ell^n; the second theorem states preservation by the arbitrary unital coefficient map. The other four declarations are the real chart-operation composites and their canonical tensor/site/shift and scalar/site natural comparisons. The ordinary module-valued-sheaf presentation and the exact Dctf predicates are those recorded on det-sp-et-proet-adjunction-transfer. The pro-etale finite Tate object is the exact comparison pullback of the finite etale Tate object, identified with the root-normalized pro-etale tensor powers by the imported finite-root comparison. No statement correction, new mathematical notion, or dependency repair.
